### `#125` (`Adv-1`) — Codeforces 724E: Goods Transportation

- **Judge / URL**: [Codeforces 724E](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/724/E) (`[EN]`)
- **Constraints**: $N \le 10^4$ cities, uniform transit capacity $c \in [0, 10^9]$, supplies $p_i \in [0, 10^9]$, demands $s_i \in [0, 10^9]$. Every city $i$ can send up to $c$ units of goods directly to every city $j > i$ ($1 \le i < j \le N$). Compute the maximum total goods delivered from $s$ to $t$.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal

This is the flagship **Direction B Flow Elimination** problem (`Section 2.2`). The network has $N = 10^4$ vertices and $\binom{N}{2} \approx 5 \cdot 10^7$ directed arcs $i \to j$ ($i < j$) of uniform capacity $c$. Building the graph is impossible; we switch to minimizing the dual $s$-$t$ cut cost $C(S)$ over all $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$.

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation

For any source-side subset $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ of cardinality $k = |S|$, our derivation in Section 2.2 gives two equivalent representations:

1. **Sequential Prefix-Count DP ($O(N^2)$)**:
   Charging each severed transit arc $u \to i$ ($u < i, u \in S, i \notin S$) to its right endpoint $i \notin S$:
   $$dp[i][k] = \min\big(dp[i-1][k] + p_i + k \cdot c,\;\; dp[i-1][k-1] + s_i\big).$$
2. **Global Cardinality Decoupling ($O(N \log N)$ Slope-Difference Greedy)**:
   Using $\big|\{(i, j) : i < j, i \in S, j \notin S\}\big| = \sum_{i \in S} (N - i) - \binom{k}{2}$, we obtain:
   $$C(S) = \sum_{i=1}^N p_i - \frac{k(k-1)}{2}c + \sum_{i \in S} \underbrace{\big(s_i - p_i + (N - i)c\big)}_{w_i}.$$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Compilation)

- **For the $O(N \log N)$ Greedy**: Compute $w_i = s_i - p_i + (N - i)c$ for $i = 1, \dots, N$, sort $w_1 \le w_2 \le \dots \le w_N$ ascending, and sweep $k = 0 \dots N$ keeping the running prefix sum $\sum_{r=1}^k w_{(r)}$.
- **For the $O(N^2)$ Rolling-Array DP**: Maintain a 1D array `dp[0..N]` initialized to `dp[0] = 0, dp[1..N] = INF`. In step $i$, update $k$ **backwards** from $i$ down to $1$:
  $$\text{dp}[k] = \min\big(\text{dp}[k] + p_i + k \cdot c,\;\; \text{dp}[k - 1] + s_i\big), \qquad \text{dp}[0] \gets \text{dp}[0] + p_i.$$

#### Step 4: Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

- **Toy Trace ($N = 3, c = 2$, $p = [5, 1, 6]$, $s = [2, 8, 3]$)**:
  - All-$T$ baseline: $\sum p_i = 12$.
  - Weights $w_i = s_i - p_i + (3 - i)\cdot 2$: $w_1 = 2 - 5 + 4 = +1$, $w_2 = 8 - 1 + 2 = +9$, $w_3 = 3 - 6 + 0 = -3$.
  - Sorted $w$: $[-3, +1, +9]$.
  - $k = 0: 12$; $k = 1: 12 - 0 + (-3) = 9$; $k = 2: 12 - 2 + (-3 + 1) = \mathbf{8}$; $k = 3: 12 - 6 + (-3 + 1 + 9) = 13$. Minimum cut is **$8$**.
- **Failure Guard (`FM-16a`)**: Never charge $c$ when $i \in S$ and $j \notin S$ for $j < i$! Only forward arcs $u \to v$ ($u < v$) exist in the DAG.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #125 (CF 724E)"}
- **Hint 1 (Diagnostic)**: Convert Max-Flow into Min-Cut: each city $i$ chooses to be on the source side $S$ or the sink side $\bar{S}$.
- **Hint 2 (Algebraic)**: When city $i$ is placed in $\bar{S}$, how many transit arcs $u \to i$ ($u < i$) are severed? Exactly $k$, the number of cities before $i$ that were placed in $S$!
- **Hint 3 (Compilation)**: Either run the 1D rolling DP `dp[k] = min(dp[k] + p[i] + k * c, dp[k-1] + s[i])` in $O(N^2)$, or use $\sum_{i \in S, j \notin S, i < j} 1 = \sum_{i \in S}(N - i) - \binom{|S|}{2}$ to sort by $w_i = s_i - p_i + (N - i)c$ in $O(N \log N)$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Complete C++ Solution for #125 (CF 724E — Both $O(N \log N)$ Greedy & $O(N^2)$ DP)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int n;
    long long c;
    if (!(cin >> n >> c)) return 0;

    vector<long long> p(n + 1), s(n + 1);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) cin >> p[i];
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) cin >> s[i];

    // Method 1: O(N log N) Algebraic Decoupling & Slope-Difference Greedy
    long long base_cut = 0;
    vector<long long> w(n);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        base_cut += p[i];
        w[i - 1] = s[i] - p[i] + (long long)(n - i) * c;
    }
    sort(w.begin(), w.end());

    long long ans = base_cut;
    long long pref_w = 0;
    for (int k = 1; k <= n; ++k) {
        pref_w += w[k - 1];
        long long pairs_in_S = (long long)k * (k - 1) / 2;
        ans = min(ans, base_cut - pairs_in_S * c + pref_w);
    }

    cout << ans << '\n';
    return 0;
}

/*

    const long long INF = 4e18;
    vector<long long> dp(n + 1, INF);
    dp[0] = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        for (int k = i; k >= 1; --k) {
            dp[k] = min(dp[k] + p[i] + (long long)k * c, dp[k - 1] + s[i]);
        }
        dp[0] += p[i];
    }
```

### `#126` (`Adv-2`) — Codeforces 1919F2: Wine Factory (Hard Version)

- **Judge / URL**: [Codeforces 1919F2](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1919/F2) (`[EN]`)
- **Constraints**: $N, Q \le 5 \cdot 10^5$, $a_i, b_i \in [0, 10^9]$, and **finite forward pipe capacities** $c_i \in [0, 10^{18}]$ for $1 \le i \le N - 1$. Given $Q$ online point updates to $(a_p, b_p, c_p)$, output the maximum wine produced after each update.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal

Unlike `#121` (`CF 1919F1`), the pipe capacities $c_i$ are now **finite**, so a minimum $s$-$t$ cut can sever any subset of forward pipes $i \to i + 1$. Because the graph is a 1D chain of treewidth $1$, the cut polynomial decomposes into a product of $2 \times 2$ $(\min, +)$ tropical matrices (`Section 2.3`).

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation

Let state $0$ denote $x_i \in \bar{S}$ (sink side $T$, paying $a_i$) and state $1$ denote $x_i \in S$ (source side $S$, paying $b_i$). Across pipe $i \xrightarrow{c_i} i + 1$, the directed cut penalty is $c_i \cdot [x_i = 1 \land x_{i+1} = 0]$.

For every Segment Tree interval $[L, R]$, define the $2 \times 2$ matrix $D_{[L, R]}(u, v)$ ($u, v \in \{0, 1\}$) as the minimum cut cost inside $[L, R]$ given boundary states $x_L = u$ and $x_R = v$:

$$
D_{[i, i]} = \begin{pmatrix} a_i & +\infty \\ +\infty & b_i \end{pmatrix}, \qquad D_{[L, R]}(u, v) = \min_{x, y \in \{0, 1\}} \Big( D_{[L, M]}(u, x) + D_{[M+1, R]}(y, v) + c_M \cdot [x = 1 \land y = 0] \Big).
$$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Compilation)

- Store a $2 \times 2$ array `long long d[2][2]` in each Segment Tree node.
- Notice that in the merge across midpoint $M$, the pipe capacity $c_M$ only participates at the single node whose midpoint is $M$! When query updates $(a_p, b_p, c_p)$, updating leaf $p$ automatically traverses every ancestor whose midpoint could be $p$ (since $p \in [L, M]$ for that ancestor).
- After each update, output $\min_{u, v \in \{0, 1\}} D_{[1, N]}(u, v)$.

#### Step 4: Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

- **Toy Trace ($N = 2$)**: Let $a = [10, 1]$, $b = [1, 10]$, and pipe $c_1 = 3$.
  - Leaf $1$: $\begin{pmatrix} 10 & \infty \\ \infty & 1 \end{pmatrix}$; Leaf $2$: $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & \infty \\ \infty & 10 \end{pmatrix}$.
  - Merged root $D_{[1, 2]}$:
    - $(0, 0)$ ($T, T$): $a_1 + a_2 = 10 + 1 = 11$.
    - $(0, 1)$ ($T, S$): $a_1 + b_2 + 0 = 10 + 10 = 20$.
    - $(1, 0)$ ($S, T$): $b_1 + a_2 + c_1 = 1 + 1 + 3 = \mathbf{5}$ (severing $1 \to t$, $s \to 2$, and pipe $1 \to 2$!).
    - $(1, 1)$ ($S, S$): $b_1 + b_2 = 1 + 10 = 11$.
  - Minimum cut is $5$.
- **Failure Guard (`FM-16a`)**: Adding $+c_M$ when $(x, y) = (0, 1)$ ($T \to S$) treats the pipe as undirected and gives $10 + 10 + 3 = 23$ on $(0, 1)$, corrupting transitions whenever $T \to S$ is optimal. Only $(x, y) = (1, 0)$ ($S \to T$) pays $c_M$!

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #126 (CF 1919F2)"}
- **Hint 1 (Diagnostic)**: When $c_i < \infty$, the cut assignment $(x_1, \dots, x_N) \in \{T, S\}^N$ can switch from $S$ to $T$ at any pipe $i \to i+1$ by paying $c_i$.
- **Hint 2 (Algebraic)**: For each segment $[L, R]$, maintain the 4 values `dp[u][v]` ($u, v \in \{0, 1\}$): the minimum cut cost on $[L, R]$ when $x_L = u$ and $x_R = v$.
- **Hint 3 (Compilation)**: When merging `[L, M]` (ending in state $x$) and `[M+1, R]` (starting in state $y$), add `c[M]` **only** when $x = 1$ ($S$) and $y = 0$ ($T$)!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Complete C++ Solution for #126 (CF 1919F2 — Wine Factory Hard Version)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

const long long INF = 4e18;

struct Mat {
    long long d[2][2];
    Mat() {
        d[0][0] = d[0][1] = d[1][0] = d[1][1] = INF;
    }
};

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int n, q;
    if (!(cin >> n >> q)) return 0;

    vector<long long> a(n + 1), b(n + 1), c(n + 1, 0);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) cin >> a[i];
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) cin >> b[i];
    for (int i = 1; i < n; ++i) cin >> c[i];

    vector<Mat> tree(4 * n + 4);

    auto merge_nodes = [&](const Mat& L, const Mat& R, long long pipe_c) {
        Mat res;
        for (int u = 0; u < 2; ++u) {
            for (int x = 0; x < 2; ++x) {
                if (L.d[u][x] >= INF) continue;
                for (int y = 0; y < 2; ++y) {
                    long long cross = (x == 1 && y == 0) ? pipe_c : 0;
                    for (int v = 0; v < 2; ++v) {
                        if (R.d[y][v] >= INF) continue;
                        res.d[u][v] = min(res.d[u][v], L.d[u][x] + R.d[y][v] + cross);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return res;
    };

    auto build = [&](auto& self, int u, int l, int r) -> void {
        if (l == r) {
            tree[u] = Mat();
            tree[u].d[0][0] = a[l]; // l in T (sink side)
            tree[u].d[1][1] = b[l]; // l in S (source side)
            return;
        }
        int mid = (l + r) / 2;
        self(self, 2 * u, l, mid);
        self(self, 2 * u + 1, mid + 1, r);
        tree[u] = merge_nodes(tree[2 * u], tree[2 * u + 1], c[mid]);
    };

    auto update = [&](auto& self, int u, int l, int r, int p) -> void {
        if (l == r) {
            tree[u] = Mat();
            tree[u].d[0][0] = a[l];
            tree[u].d[1][1] = b[l];
            return;
        }
        int mid = (l + r) / 2;
        if (p <= mid) self(self, 2 * u, l, mid, p);
        else self(self, 2 * u + 1, mid + 1, r, p);
        tree[u] = merge_nodes(tree[2 * u], tree[2 * u + 1], c[mid]);
    };

    build(build, 1, 1, n);

    while (q--) {
        int p;
        long long x, y, z;
        cin >> p >> x >> y >> z;
        a[p] = x;
        b[p] = y;
        if (p < n) c[p] = z;
        update(update, 1, 1, n, p);

        long long ans = INF;
        for (int u = 0; u < 2; ++u)
            for (int v = 0; v < 2; ++v)
                ans = min(ans, tree[1].d[u][v]);
        cout << ans << '\n';
    }
    return 0;
}
```

### `#127` (`Mas-1`) — Codeforces 343E: Pumping Stations

- **Judge / URL**: [Codeforces 343E](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/343/E) (`[EN]`)
- **Constraints**: Undirected weighted graph with $N \le 200$ vertices and $M \le 1000$ edges. Find a permutation $\pi = (\pi_1, \pi_2, \dots, \pi_N)$ of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ maximizing $\sum_{i=1}^{N-1} \operatorname{MinCut}_G(\pi_i, \pi_{i+1})$, and output both the maximum sum and the optimal permutation $\pi$.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal

We want a maximum-weight Hamiltonian path in the complete graph of pairwise minimum cuts $\lambda_G(u, v)$. While Maximum Travelling Salesman is NP-hard on general metrics, $\lambda_G(u, v)$ is an **ultrametric tree-bottleneck function** on the Gomory–Hu tree $T_{\text{GH}}$!

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation & Exact Upper Bound Proof

Let $T_{\text{GH}} = (V, E_T, w_T)$ be the Gomory–Hu tree of $G$. We prove that for **any** permutation $\pi$, its objective is bounded above by the total weight of $T_{\text{GH}}$, and that this upper bound is **always achievable**:

$$
\max_{\pi \in S_N} \sum_{i=1}^{N-1} \lambda_G(\pi_i, \pi_{i+1}) = \sum_{e \in E_T} w_T(e).
$$

*Proof of Upper Bound & Constructive Equality*:

1. **Upper Bound ($\le$)**: Consider the **minimum-weight edge** $e_{\min} \in \arg\min_{e \in E_T} w_T(e)$ of $T_{\text{GH}}$. Removing $e_{\min}$ splits $T_{\text{GH}}$ into two subtrees $T_1$ and $T_2$. Any permutation $\pi_1, \dots, \pi_N$ must step between $V(T_1)$ and $V(T_2)$ at least once, and that step uses $e_{\min}$ on its tree path, paying $\le w_T(e_{\min})$. More generally, mapping each adjacent step $(\pi_i, \pi_{i+1})$ to a bottleneck edge on $P_T(\pi_i, \pi_{i+1})$ via induction on $|V|$ shows $\sum_{i=1}^{N-1} \lambda_G(\pi_i, \pi_{i+1}) \le \sum_{e \in E_T} w_T(e)$.
2. **Constructive Equality ($=$)**: Suppose we order **all vertices of $T_1$ first**, followed by **all vertices of $T_2$**. Because $e_{\min}$ is the *globally lightest* edge in the entire tree $T_{\text{GH}}$, for *any* last vertex $x \in V(T_1)$ and *any* first vertex $y \in V(T_2)$, the path $P_T(x, y)$ crosses $e_{\min}$ and every other edge on $P_T(x, y)$ has weight $\ge w_T(e_{\min})$! Therefore, the boundary transition $(x, y)$ between $T_1$ and $T_2$ achieves bottleneck **exactly $w_T(e_{\min})$**! Applying the exact same rule recursively to $T_1$ and $T_2$ achieves $\sum_{e \in E_T} w_T(e)$! $\blacksquare$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Kruskal DSU Concatenation)

Splitting $T_{\text{GH}}$ top-down at the minimum-weight edge $e_{\min}$ is bottom-up equivalent to **Kruskal's DSU in descending order of edge weights**!

- Build $T_{\text{GH}}$ in $N - 1$ Dinic calls using Gusfield's algorithm.
- Sort the $N - 1$ edges of $T_{\text{GH}}$ in **descending** order of $w_T(e)$.
- Maintain a DSU where each component $c$ stores an ordered list `order[c]` of its vertices (initially `order[u] = {u}`).
- For each tree edge $e = (u, v)$ from heaviest to lightest: append `order[find(v)]` to the end of `order[find(u)]` and unite the two components! At the end, the single list `order[find(1)]` is the exact optimal permutation $\pi$!

#### Step 4: Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

- **Failure Guard**: Splitting at an arbitrary edge (or sorting edges ascending instead of **descending** in DSU) fails because when two components are concatenated across a heavy edge $e$, a *lighter* edge already inside one of the components would become the bottleneck on $P_T(x, y)$ instead of $e$!

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #127 (CF 343E)"}
- **Hint 1 (Diagnostic)**: Build the Gomory–Hu tree $T_{\text{GH}}$. Why can no permutation ever exceed the sum of the $N - 1$ edge weights of $T_{\text{GH}}$?
- **Hint 2 (Algebraic)**: Let $e_{\min}$ be the *lightest* edge in $T_{\text{GH}}$, splitting $T_{\text{GH}}$ into $T_1$ and $T_2$. If you visit all of $T_1$ and then all of $T_2$, what is the bottleneck between the last node of $T_1$ and the first node of $T_2$? Always $w_T(e_{\min})$!
- **Hint 3 (Compilation)**: Sort the $N - 1$ edges of $T_{\text{GH}}$ in **descending** order of weight and merge component vertex lists using a Disjoint Set Union (DSU)!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Complete C++ Solution for #127 (CF 343E — Pumping Stations)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

const int INF = 1e9;

struct Dinic {
    struct Edge {
        int to, rev, cap, init_cap;
    };
    int n;
    vector<vector<Edge>> adj;
    vector<int> level, ptr;

    Dinic(int n) : n(n), adj(n + 1), level(n + 1), ptr(n + 1) {}

    void add_undirected_edge(int u, int v, int c) {
        adj[u].push_back({v, (int)adj[v].size(), c, c});
        adj[v].push_back({u, (int)adj[u].size() - 1, c, c});
    }

    void reset() {
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i)
            for (auto& e : adj[i]) e.cap = e.init_cap;
    }

    bool bfs(int s, int t) {
        fill(level.begin(), level.end(), -1);
        level[s] = 0;
        queue<int> q;
        q.push(s);
        while (!q.empty()) {
            int u = q.front();
            q.pop();
            for (auto& e : adj[u]) {
                if (e.cap > 0 && level[e.to] == -1) {
                    level[e.to] = level[u] + 1;
                    q.push(e.to);
                }
            }
        }
        return level[t] != -1;
    }

    int dfs(int u, int t, int pushed) {
        if (pushed == 0 || u == t) return pushed;
        for (int& cid = ptr[u]; cid < (int)adj[u].size(); ++cid) {
            auto& e = adj[u][cid];
            if (level[u] + 1 != level[e.to] || e.cap == 0) continue;
            int tr = dfs(e.to, t, min(pushed, e.cap));
            if (tr == 0) continue;
            e.cap -= tr;
            adj[e.to][e.rev].cap += tr;
            return tr;
        }
        return 0;
    }

    int max_flow(int s, int t) {
        reset();
        int flow = 0;
        while (bfs(s, t)) {
            fill(ptr.begin(), ptr.end(), 0);
            while (int pushed = dfs(s, t, INF)) flow += pushed;
        }
        return flow;
    }
};

struct TreeEdge {
    int u, v, w;
    bool operator<(const TreeEdge& other) const {
        return w > other.w; // Sort descending!
    }
};

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int n, m;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m)) return 0;

    Dinic dinic(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
        int u, v, w;
        cin >> u >> v >> w;
        dinic.add_undirected_edge(u, v, w);
    }

    vector<int> p(n + 1, 1);
    vector<TreeEdge> tree_edges;
    long long total_weight = 0;

    for (int s = 2; s <= n; ++s) {
        int t = p[s];
        int w = dinic.max_flow(s, t);
        total_weight += w;
        tree_edges.push_back({s, t, w});
        for (int u = s + 1; u <= n; ++u) {
            if (p[u] == t && dinic.level[u] != -1) {
                p[u] = s;
            }
        }
    }

    sort(tree_edges.begin(), tree_edges.end());

    vector<int> dsu(n + 1);
    vector<vector<int>> comp_order(n + 1);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        dsu[i] = i;
        comp_order[i] = {i};
    }

    auto find_set = [&](auto& self, int x) -> int {
        return dsu[x] == x ? x : dsu[x] = self(self, dsu[x]);
    };

    for (const auto& e : tree_edges) {
        int ru = find_set(find_set, e.u);
        int rv = find_set(find_set, e.v);
        if (ru != rv) {
            comp_order[ru].insert(comp_order[ru].end(),
                                  comp_order[rv].begin(), comp_order[rv].end());
            comp_order[rv].clear();
            dsu[rv] = ru;
        }
    }

    int root = find_set(find_set, 1);
    cout << total_weight << '\n';
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        cout << comp_order[root][i] << (i + 1 == n ? '\n' : ' ');
    }
    return 0;
}
```

### `#128` (`Mas-2`) — Codeforces 903G: Yet Another MaxFlow Problem

- **Judge / URL**: [Codeforces 903G](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/903/G) (`[EN]`)
- **Constraints**: $N, M, Q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$. Directed left chain $A_1 \xrightarrow{x_1} A_2 \xrightarrow{x_2} \dots \xrightarrow{x_{N-1}} A_N$, directed right chain $B_1 \xrightarrow{y_1} B_2 \xrightarrow{y_2} \dots \xrightarrow{y_{N-1}} B_N$, and $M$ directed cross-edges $A_u \xrightarrow{z_e} B_v$. Output $\operatorname{MaxFlow}(A_1, B_N)$ initially and after each of $Q$ point updates changing a single left-chain capacity $x_i$.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal

We have two coupled forward chains of length $N = 2 \cdot 10^5$ with $Q = 2 \cdot 10^5$ updates to $x_i$. Crucially, notice two facts (`Section 2.4`):

1. Because all edges on $A_1 \to \dots \to A_N$ and $B_1 \to \dots \to B_N$ point forward from $s = A_1$ toward $t = B_N$, any minimal $A_1$-$B_N$ cut puts a **contiguous prefix** $\{A_1, \dots, A_i\}$ ($1 \le i \le N$, paying $x_i$ with $x_N = 0$) and a **contiguous prefix** $\{B_1, \dots, B_j\}$ ($0 \le j \le N - 1$, paying $y_j$ with $y_0 = 0$) on the source side $S$!
2. The $Q$ online queries **only modify $x_i$**—they never modify $y_j$ or the cross-edges $z_e$!

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation

For a chosen left cut index $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ ($A_1 \dots A_i \in S$) and right cut index $j \in \{0, \dots, N - 1\}$ ($B_1 \dots B_j \in S$, $B_{j+1} \dots B_N \in T$), a cross-edge $A_u \to B_v$ of capacity $z_{uv}$ crosses from $S$ to $T$ if and only if $u \le i$ and $v > j$ (i.e., $j \in [0, v - 1]$):

$$
\operatorname{Cut}(i, j) = x_i + \underbrace{\left( y_j + \sum_{u \le i,\; v > j} z_{uv} \right)}_{f_i(j)}, \qquad \operatorname{MaxFlow}(A_1, B_N) = \min_{1 \le i \le N} \big(x_i + C_i\big),
$$

where $C_i = \min_{0 \le j \le N - 1} f_i(j)$ is completely independent of $x$ and can be **precomputed once** for all $i = 1, \dots, N$!

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Sweep-Line Lazy Segment Tree)

- **Phase 1 (Precomputing $C_1, \dots, C_N$ in $O((N + M) \log N)$)**:
  - Build a Lazy Range-Add Range-Min Segment Tree over $j \in [0, N - 1]$, initialized at leaf $j$ with $y_j$ ($y_0 = 0$).
  - Sweep $i$ from $1$ to $N$: for each cross-edge $A_i \to B_v$ of weight $z$, add $+z$ to the prefix range $j \in [0, v - 1]$ in the Segment Tree!
  - After processing all cross-edges out of $A_i$, query the global minimum of the Segment Tree and store it as $C_i = \text{seg.root\_min}()$.
- **Phase 2 (Answering $Q$ Updates to $x_i$ in $O(Q \log N)$)**:
  - Maintain the $N$ values $x_i + C_i$ in a `std::multiset<long long>` (or a second point-update Segment Tree), updating $x_i + C_i$ in $O(\log N)$ per query!

#### Step 4: Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

- **Failure Guard**: Do not forget $j = 0$ ($y_0 = 0$, placing **all** $B_1, \dots, B_N$ on the sink side $T$) and $i = N$ ($x_N = 0$, placing **all** $A_1, \dots, A_N$ on the source side $S$)! If $j = 0$ is omitted from the Segment Tree domain $[0, N - 1]$, any cut that leaves $B_1 \in T$ (which is required whenever $A_i \to B_1$ is severed!) will be missed.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints for #128 (CF 903G)"}
- **Hint 1 (Diagnostic)**: Why does an optimal cut never sever more than one edge $A_i \to A_{i+1}$ on the $A$-chain and one edge $B_j \to B_{j+1}$ on the $B$-chain?
- **Hint 2 (Algebraic)**: For a fixed $A$-prefix $A_1 \dots A_i \in S$ and $B$-prefix $B_1 \dots B_j \in S$, each cross-edge $A_u \to B_v$ is cut iff $u \le i$ and $j \le v - 1$. Notice that the queries never change $y_j$ or the cross-edges!
- **Hint 3 (Compilation)**: Sweep $i = 1 \dots N$ and use a Lazy Range-Add Range-Min Segment Tree over $j \in [0, N - 1]$ to precompute $C_i = \min_j (y_j + \sum_{u \le i, v > j} z_{uv})$. Then maintain $\min_i (x_i + C_i)$ under point updates to $x_i$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Complete C++ Solution for #128 (CF 903G — Yet Another MaxFlow Problem)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

const long long INF = 4e18;

struct LazySegTree {
    int n;
    vector<long long> mn, lz;

    LazySegTree(int n) : n(n), mn(4 * n + 4, 0), lz(4 * n + 4, 0) {}

    void build(int u, int l, int r, const vector<long long>& y) {
        if (l == r) {
            mn[u] = y[l];
            return;
        }
        int mid = (l + r) / 2;
        build(2 * u, l, mid, y);
        build(2 * u + 1, mid + 1, r, y);
        mn[u] = min(mn[2 * u], mn[2 * u + 1]);
    }

    void apply(int u, long long v) {
        mn[u] += v;
        lz[u] += v;
    }

    void push(int u) {
        if (lz[u] != 0) {
            apply(2 * u, lz[u]);
            apply(2 * u + 1, lz[u]);
            lz[u] = 0;
        }
    }

    void range_add(int u, int l, int r, int ql, int qr, long long v) {
        if (ql <= l && r <= qr) {
            apply(u, v);
            return;
        }
        push(u);
        int mid = (l + r) / 2;
        if (ql <= mid) range_add(2 * u, l, mid, ql, qr, v);
        if (qr > mid) range_add(2 * u + 1, mid + 1, r, ql, qr, v);
        mn[u] = min(mn[2 * u], mn[2 * u + 1]);
    }
};

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int n, m, q;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m >> q)) return 0;

    vector<long long> x(n + 1, 0), y(n, 0);
    for (int i = 1; i < n; ++i) {
        cin >> x[i] >> y[i];
    }

    vector<vector<pair<int, long long>>> cross(n + 1);
    for (int i = 0; i < m; ++i) {
        int u, v;
        long long z;
        cin >> u >> v >> z;
        cross[u].push_back({v, z});
    }

    // Phase 1: Sweep i = 1 .. N to precompute optimal B-cut C[i]
    LazySegTree seg_b(n);
    seg_b.build(1, 0, n - 1, y);

    vector<long long> C(n + 1, 0);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        for (auto& [v, z] : cross[i]) {
            seg_b.range_add(1, 0, n - 1, 0, v - 1, z);
        }
        C[i] = seg_b.mn[1];
    }

    // Phase 2: Maintain min_{1 <= i <= N} (x[i] + C[i]) under point updates to x[i]
    multiset<long long> active_cuts;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        active_cuts.insert(x[i] + C[i]);
    }

    cout << *active_cuts.begin() << '\n';
    while (q--) {
        int idx;
        long long w;
        cin >> idx >> w;
        active_cuts.erase(active_cuts.find(x[idx] + C[idx]));
        x[idx] = w;
        active_cuts.insert(x[idx] + C[idx]);
        cout << *active_cuts.begin() << '\n';
    }
    return 0;
}
```
::::

## 7. Pre-Submission Checklist (`FM-16` & `FM-16a` Audit)

Before submitting any Direction B Min-Cut DP, Stoer–Wagner, or Gomory–Hu Cut Tree solution, run through this 6-point verification audit:

1. **Directed Cut Asymmetry Audit (`FM-16a`)**:
   In any Direction B Min-Cut DP or $(\min, +)$ matrix transition (`CF 724E`, `CF 1919F2`, `CF 903G`), verify that a directed edge $u \to v$ of capacity $c_{uv}$ pays $c_{uv}$ **only when $u \in S$ and $v \in T$**, and pays **$0$** when $u \in T$ and $v \in S$.
2. **Boundary Index Completeness (`k = 0` and `k = N`)**:
   In prefix-suffix cut parameterizations (`CF 1919F1`, `CF 903G`, `ARC 125E`), confirm that both extreme cuts—putting **all** vertices in $S$ (`k = 0` or `i = N`, $x_N = 0$) and putting **all** vertices in $T$ (`j = 0`, $y_0 = 0$)—are included in the DP or Segment Tree domain.
3. **Gusfield Star-Splitting Scope Guard (`FM-16`)**:
   In Gusfield's loop (`for u = s+1 .. N`), confirm that you check `if (p[u] == t && vis[u]) p[u] = s;` (or in a Cut-Equivalent tree over all $u \neq s, t$, `if (p[u] == t && vis[u])`). Never re-parent vertices whose current parent is not $t$.
4. **Full Uncontracted Graph Reset in Gomory–Hu**:
   Before each of the $N - 1$ Dinic runs in Gusfield's algorithm, reset **all** edge capacities back to their initial undirected capacities $(c, c)$ on the **complete original graph $G$**—never delete vertices outside the current bucket.
5. **Undirected Graph Prerequisite for Gomory–Hu & Stoer–Wagner**:
   Confirm that the input graph $G$ is **undirected** ($w_{uv} = w_{vu}$). If $G$ is directed, neither Stoer–Wagner nor Gomory–Hu applies.
6. **Parallel Edge Accumulation in Stoer–Wagner**:
   When reading edges into an adjacency matrix for Stoer–Wagner (`POJ 2914`) and when contracting $t$ into $s$, always accumulate `g[u][v] += w` rather than overwriting `g[u][v] = w`.

## 8. Chapter Summary & Bridge to Part IV Checkpoint (`CP-IV`)

### Chapter 16 Revision Summary

- **Direction B Flow Elimination (`最大流转最小割 DP`)**: When $N \ge 10^4$ or dynamic queries $Q \ge 10^5$ prohibit augmenting paths, replace $\operatorname{MaxFlow}(s, t)$ with $\min_{S \subseteq V} C(S)$ and compress the $2^N$ cut space via cardinality DP (`CF 724E`), sorted slope-difference greedy ($w_i = s_i - p_i + (N - i)c$), $2 \times 2$ $(\min, +)$ tropical matrix Segment Trees (`CF 1919F2`), or prefix-suffix sweep-line Segment Trees (`CF 903G`).
- **Stoer–Wagner Global Minimum Cut**: By active-vertex cut induction along a Maximum Adjacency Search (`MAS`) ordering $v_1, \dots, v_N$, the last two vertices $(s, t) = (v_{N-1}, v_N)$ satisfy $\lambda_G(s, t) = w(A_{N-1}, t)$. Contracting $s$ and $t$ across $N - 1$ phases computes $\lambda(G)$ in $O(VE + V^2 \log V)$ or $O(V^3)$ time.
- **Gomory–Hu Cut Trees & Gusfield's Star-Splitting (`最小割树`)**: By Symmetric Submodularity and the Cut Uncrossing Lemma, all $\binom{N}{2}$ pairwise minimum cuts of an undirected graph are encoded as path bottlenecks on a single $N$-vertex tree $T_{\text{GH}}$ built in $N - 1$ Dinic calls on the uncontracted graph $G$.

### Part IV Two-Stage Blind Diagnostic Checkpoint (`CP-IV`: `#217`–`#224`)

This checkpoint tests your diagnostic mastery across all of **Part IV (Chapters 14–16)**: 0-1 Fractional Programming & Maximum Density Subgraphs (`Ch 14`), Planar Dual Shortest Paths & Coarea Duality (`Ch 15`), and Direction B Min-Cut DP & Gomory–Hu Cut Trees (`Ch 16`)—mixed with **3 lookalike decoys** that do *not* require network flow or cut compression!

#### Stage 1: Scrambled Blind Problem Statements (5 Genuine + 3 Decoys)

- **`#217` (`CP-IV-1`)**: Given a tree $T = (V, E)$ with $N \le 2 \cdot 10^5$ vertices where each vertex $u$ has source capacity $s \xrightarrow{a_u} u$, sink capacity $u \xrightarrow{b_u} t$, and each tree edge $\{u, v\}$ has undirected capacity $c_{uv}$, compute $\operatorname{MaxFlow}(s, t)$.
- **`#218` (`CP-IV-2`)**: Given $N \le 10^5$ items with values $v_i > 0$ and weights $w_i > 0$, select **exactly $K$ items** to maximize $\frac{\sum_{i \in S} v_i}{\sum_{i \in S} w_i}$.
- **`#219` (`CP-IV-3`)**: Given an $N \times M$ planar grid ($N, M \le 600$) where every horizontal and vertical edge has capacity $c_e \ge 0$, $s$ is the entire top row, and $t$ is the entire bottom row, compute $\operatorname{MaxFlow}(s, t)$.
- **`#220` (`CP-IV-4`)**: Given an undirected weighted graph $G = (V, E, w)$ ($N \le 2000, M \le 5000$), answer $Q \le 10^5$ queries asking for the maximum bottleneck capacity of a **single simple path** between $u$ and $v$.
- **`#221` (`CP-IV-5`)**: Given an $N \times N$ symmetric non-negative matrix $M_{u,v}$ ($N \le 1000$), determine whether there exists an undirected capacitated graph $G = (V, E, w)$ such that $\operatorname{MinCut}_G(u, v) = M_{u,v}$ for all $u \neq v$.
- **`#222` (`CP-IV-6`)**: Given $N \le 300$ projects with profits $p_i > 0$, time costs $t_i > 0$, and prerequisite dependencies $u \to v$, find a non-empty closed set of projects $C$ maximizing $\frac{\sum_{i \in C} p_i}{\sum_{i \in C} t_i}$.
- **`#223` (`CP-IV-7`)**: Given an undirected connected planar graph $G = (V, E, w)$ ($N \le 10^5$) with positive edge weights $w_e > 0$, find a spanning tree of $G$ of minimum total weight.
- **`#224` (`CP-IV-8`)**: Given a complete DAG on $\{1, \dots, N\}$ ($N \le 5000$) where every forward arc $i \to j$ ($1 \le i < j \le N$) has capacity $b_j$ (depending on the destination $j$), $s \to i$ has capacity $p_i$, and $i \to t$ has capacity $s_i$, compute $\operatorname{MaxFlow}(s, t)$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Stage 2: Diagnostic Resolution & Decoy Elimination Key for CP-IV (#217–#224)"}
| ID | Verdict | Target Paradigm & Diagnostic Explanation |
| :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`#217`** | **Genuine (`Ch 16 §2.4`)** | **Direction B Tree Min-Cut DP**: At $N = 2 \cdot 10^5$, Dinic is too slow, but $\operatorname{MinCut}(s, t)$ on a tree is solved in **$O(N)$ time** via 2-state bottom-up Tree DP (`dp[u][0]` for $u \in T$, `dp[u][1]` for $u \in S$)! |
| **`#218`** | **DECOY (Binary Search + Sort)** | **Unconstrained 0-1 Fractional Knapsack**: There are **zero graph dependencies** between items! Binary search $\lambda$ and greedily pick the $K$ items with the largest shifted weights $v_i - \lambda w_i$ in $O(N \log N \log V)$. |
| **`#219`** | **Genuine (`Ch 15 §2`)** | **Top-to-Bottom Planar Grid Minimum Cut**: Contracting the top row into $s$ and the bottom row into $t$ places both terminals on the outer boundary; run **Planar Dual Dijkstra** from the Left Outer Face $S^*$ to the Right Outer Face $T^*$ in $O(NM \log(NM))$! |
| **`#220`** | **DECOY (Maximum Spanning Tree)** | **Single-Path Bottleneck $\neq$ Gomory–Hu Cut Tree**: A single path's bottleneck capacity is maximized by the path minimum on the **Maximum Spanning Tree** (Kruskal in $O(M \log M)$), NOT $N - 1$ max-flows! |
| **`#221`** | **Genuine (`Ch 16 §4.1`)** | **Ultrametric Realizability of Gomory–Hu Cut Matrices**: By Corollary 16.3, $M$ is realizable as $\lambda_G(u, v)$ iff $M_{u,w} \ge \min(M_{u,v}, M_{v,w})$ for all $u, v, w$, which holds iff $M$ equals the path-bottleneck matrix of its own **Maximum Spanning Tree** $T^*$ (checked in $O(N^2)$)! |
| **`#222`** | **Genuine (`Ch 14 + Ch 09`)** | **0-1 Fractional Project Selection**: Binary search (or Dinkelbach) trial ratio $\lambda > 0$; assign each project net weight $w_i(\lambda) = p_i - \lambda t_i$ and solve Maximum Weight Closure (`Ch 09`) at each step. |
| **`#223`** | **DECOY (Kruskal / Prim MST)** | **Minimum Spanning Tree**: Planarity does not turn MST into a flow problem—Kruskal/Prim (or linear-time planar MST) solves it directly without cuts. |
| **`#224`** | **Genuine (`Ch 16 §2.2`)** | **Head-Weighted Complete DAG Min-Cut DP**: By Direction B (`§2.2`), $C(S) = \sum_{i \notin S} p_i + \sum_{i \in S} s_i + \sum_{j \notin S} \big|S \cap \{1, \dots, j-1\}\big| \cdot b_j$. Scanning $i = 1 \dots N$ and tracking $k = \big|S \cap \{1, \dots, i\}\big|$ gives $dp[i][k] = \min(dp[i-1][k] + p_i + k \cdot b_i,\; dp[i-1][k-1] + s_i)$ in $O(N^2)$ time! |
::::

### Bridge to Part V: Min-Cost Max-Flow (MCMF), Equation Differencing & LP Duality (`Ch 17`–`Ch 21`)

Across Parts I through IV (`Chapters 1–16`), every problem had a single scalar capacity per edge: we sought either a maximum flow or a minimum cut. Starting in **[Chapter 17 — Potentials, Reduced Costs, Primal–Dual Slope Convexity & Negative-Cycle Saturation](ch17-mcmf-foundations-potentials-slope-negative-cycles.qmd)**, every edge acquires a second dimension—a **unit cost $w_e$**—opening the rich world of Min-Cost Max-Flow (MCMF), Johnson potentials, piecewise-linear convex slope curves $C(f)$, equation differencing (`差分约束与连续守恒方程差分`), and Linear Programming Duality.
